summary: Migration 0003 drops ngiab_modelrun with no reverse path. The destructive step is explicitly acknowledged in the migration docstring and README (downgrade unsupported, back up ~/.ngiab_visualizer_db). Data rescue is delegated to management/commands/backfill_manifests.py, run before `tethys db migrate` in scripts/ngiab-entrypoint.sh under `set -euo pipefail`. The command is well-engineered: idempotent, raw-SQL (survives model deletion), tolerant of a missing table (fresh installs) or an already-empty table, and it hard-fails (CommandError -> non-zero exit -> migrate never runs) when a manifest write itself fails (e.g. read-only storage). Test coverage in tests/test_backfill.py is unusually thorough and exercises the exact upgrade scenario the author hit in production (host paths that don't resolve inside the container, resolved by the basename fallback in _resolve()).

findings.title: DeleteModel has no runtime guard against running without backfill_manifests first
findings.detail: tethysapp/ngiab/migrations/0003_delete_modelrun.py is a pure DeleteModel with no RunPython precondition. Data safety depends entirely on scripts/ngiab-entrypoint.sh's ordering (backfill_manifests before `tethys db migrate`). Any invocation path that runs migrate without first going through that exact entrypoint script -- e.g. `docker exec <container> tethys db migrate` for troubleshooting, a future split of migration into its own init step/job, or a CMD override -- drops the table against the persistent volume with zero manifests written and no way back. The Dockerfile's own build-time `tethys db migrate` (line 48) is safe because it runs against a throwaway image-local sqlite file, not the mounted volume, but that safety is coincidental to this migration, not enforced by it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a RunPython step ahead of DeleteModel that raises if ngiab_modelrun has rows whose directories have no manifest.json yet (mirroring backfill_manifests' own resolution logic), so a bypass of the entrypoint script fails the migration instead of silently destroying data. At minimum, document prominently (README/ops runbook) that migrate must never be run standalone against a volume with real data.

findings.title: Rows resolved to a missing or out-of-root directory are permanently dropped with only a warning, not a hard stop
findings.detail: In backfill_manifests.py's handle() loop, a directory that no longer exists (line 62-69) or resolves outside run_store.local_root() (line 71-79) is counted and reported to stderr but does not raise, does not affect the exit code, and does not block the subsequent `tethys db migrate`. Once 0003 runs, those rows -- and the ids/labels they held -- are gone forever. This is a deliberate, documented tradeoff (README's 'Upgrading from an earlier version' section warns operators to move out-of-root runs first), but there is no machine-checkable signal (e.g. a non-zero/soft-fail exit code or a --strict flag) that an automated deploy pipeline could use to pause before the drop when N runs would be lost, so the only real depended-guard is a human reading container startup logs during an unattended restart.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an optional strict mode (or make missing/outside a nonzero exit unless an explicit --allow-loss flag is passed) so unattended upgrades halt rather than silently proceeding to drop rows that were never converted to a manifest.

findings.title: Basename fallback in _resolve() can merge two unrelated registry rows onto the same directory
findings.detail: _resolve() (lines 145-173) falls back to matching purely on os.path.basename(stored_real) inside the storage root when the stored path doesn't exist in the container. The migration's own docstring records that in the real production upgrade 'all five rows held host paths' that didn't resolve -- exactly the condition that triggers this fallback. If two distinct registered paths (e.g. from two different host mounts, or two imports of similarly-named runs) share a basename and only one directory with that name exists in the storage root, both rows' UUIDs are merged onto that single directory's manifest via _group_by_directory, silently attributing the wrong run's legacy shared-link ids to it. No test exercises two stale rows sharing a basename (tests/test_backfill.py only covers one stale row per basename).
findings.suggested_fix: When more than one distinct stored path resolves to the same basename candidate, skip the fallback (or flag it loudly as ambiguous) instead of silently merging both rows' ids onto one directory. Add a regression test for two stale rows sharing a basename.

findings.title: ModelRun.subset and ModelRun.tags are dropped by the migration with no carry-over into the manifest
findings.detail: The raw SQL SELECT in _registry_rows() (line 116) reads only id, label, path, teehr_configuration_name, created -- it omits subset and tags, both real columns on the model being deleted. tethysapp/ngiab/utils.py:119 documents this as intentional ('nothing ever wrote tags, and subset was settable only through register_run and read by nothing'), but the now-deleted management/commands/register_run.py did accept and persist a --subset value (confirmed via `git show d283373:.../register_run.py`), so any production row registered with a non-empty subset loses that value irrecoverably once 0003 runs. The claim that nothing read it holds for the current codebase, but it is an unverifiable assumption about existing production data (the author reports 5 real runs) rather than a technical guarantee.
findings.suggested_fix: Before running the migration against production, run `SELECT DISTINCT subset FROM ngiab_modelrun` (or equivalent) to confirm no run actually has a non-empty subset; if any do, either carry it into the manifest as an extra field or document the loss explicitly in the release notes.

residual_risks: Downgrading after 0003 is explicitly unsupported (an older image's code expects ngiab_modelrun, which is gone); the only recovery path is restoring a backup of ~/.ngiab_visualizer_db taken before the upgrade, which is documented in README but not automated or verified at migration time.

backfill_manifests' safety net (raising CommandError on write failure) only covers the write step; a directory that resolves to 'missing' or 'outside the storage root' is not covered by that hard stop and the table is dropped anyway for those rows (see finding above).
The entire rescue design assumes scripts/ngiab-entrypoint.sh is the only path by which `tethys db migrate` reaches a volume containing real data; nothing in the migration itself enforces that.
testing_gaps: No test covers two distinct stale registry rows whose basenames collide inside the storage root (the merge-onto-wrong-directory scenario in _resolve()).

No test verifies the actual shell-level exit code / set -e behavior of scripts/ngiab-entrypoint.sh when backfill_manifests fails -- coverage stops at asserting CommandError is raised inside Django's call_command, not that the container process itself halts before invoking `tethys db migrate`.

No test asserts that a row with a non-empty subset or tags value is reported or preserved in some form; the current tests only assert subset/tags are absent from the resulting entry (tests/test_registry_listing.py), which encodes the loss as expected behavior rather than testing for it.
